transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, ever since I had to move into this new place—it's just a busted-up room, really—I haven't been myself. I'm snapping at people all the time. I spend half the night up trying to fix leaks or get the heat working, and then I'm just dragging myself into work late. And once I'm there, I'm messing up stuff on the site that I normally handle with my eyes closed. It's just getting to be too much.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you moved into the new place?

Not really sad, no. I mean... I'm not sitting around crying or anything like that. It's more just that I'm really frustrated and stressed out. Maybe a little bummed when things keep breaking on me, but mostly I'm just aggravated and tired of dealing with it all.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since you moved into the new place?

Not really anxious, no. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying or feeling nervous about things. It's not like that. I guess I'm just... mostly annoyed. Like I said before, it's just frustrating dealing with the place falling apart all the time. But I wouldn't say I feel on edge or panicky or anything like that.
Do you find yourself getting angry or irritated more easily than you used to?

Yeah, definitely. Like I said earlier, I'm just snapping at people all the time now. It really doesn't take much to set me off lately. Just... little things on the job site or whatever, I just lose my patience way faster than I ever used to.
Have you been avoiding certain places or situations because of how you've been feeling lately?

No, not really. I still go to work and do what I need to do every day. I'm not hiding out or staying away from any specific places or anything like that. I'm just... in a bad mood while I'm doing it, I guess. But I haven't been avoiding anything.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping due to racing thoughts or worry?
No, my sleep's been fine. I mean, I'm tired at the end of the day from work, so I usually just crash out. I don't lay there thinking about stuff or worrying. Once I'm asleep, I'm asleep.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Yeah, I'd say so. I mean... I still like doing the same stuff I usually do. On the weekends I'll still watch the game or hang out with my buddies. I haven't really lost interest in any of that. Like I said, I'm just in a worse mood lately, but I still enjoy my regular stuff when I get around to it.
Do you feel like your irritability and frustration are directly related to the problems you're having with your new place?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, that's really why I came in. Ever since I moved into that busted-up room, I've just been snapping at people left and right. I end up staying up half the night trying to fix leaks or get the heat working, and then... well, I'm dragging myself in late to work. And because of all that, I'm messing up stuff on the job that I normally handle with no problem. So, yeah, it's all coming directly from dealing with that place.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems since you moved into the new place?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My stomach's fine, and I don't really get headaches. I mean, I'm tired, obviously, from being up so late messing with the house, but physically... nah, I feel okay.
How long have you been feeling this way since you moved into the new place?
It's been going on for about a month now. Pretty much started shortly after I moved into that room in Bridgeport.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or memories about the stressful situation with your new place that you can't seem to get out of your head?

No, not really. I mean, I think about it when I'm there, trying to fix things, or when I'm tired at work because of it. But it's not like... it's not like I'm having flashbacks or can't stop thinking about it when I'm doing other stuff. It's just a huge pain to deal with when I have to deal with it.
Have you been having any periods where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes and includes symptoms like palpitations or shortness of breath?
No, nothing like that. I don't get panic attacks or anything. I just get frustrated with the whole situation, but my heart's not racing or anything crazy like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since you started feeling this way?

No, not really. Things are pretty much the same with them. I still see my buddies and talk to my family just like before. I mean, I might complain about the room a bit more when I'm around them now, but... no, nothing's really changed between us.
Have you noticed any significant impact on your work performance or overall daily functioning due to your current frustrations?

Yeah, it actually has. Um... my foreman actually pulled me aside recently. He told me I could lose my shot at moving up to crew lead if I keep slipping on the job. It's just... I've already messed up some work paperwork and had some scheduling problems because my head's been so wrapped up in dealing with all this. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way at work.
Do you think you would go back to feeling like your normal self if the problems with your new place were resolved?

Yeah, I really think I would. I mean, the whole housing mess hasn't actually ended yet. I'm still living in that room, still trying to get the landlord to actually fix things. So it's not like the problem is over and I'm just hanging onto it. If I could just get it sorted out or get out of there, I think I'd be back to my normal self, yeah.
Have you been experiencing any excessive worry about things beyond just your current living situation?

No, not really. It's pretty much just the room. I mean, I don't really sit around worrying about other stuff. It's just... this whole housing thing is always on my mind because it's right there in front of me every day. But besides that, no, I'm not really worrying about anything else.
Have you been having any persistent and pervasive feelings of apprehension or unease that are not limited to your current living situation?

No, I don't think so. Um... I'm not just walking around feeling nervous or on edge for no reason. Like I was saying, it's really just tied to the mess with my room and the landlord. I don't really have that kind of unease about anything else.

Do you think the frustration and irritability you've been experiencing would completely go away if your living situation improved, or would you still have some lingering concerns or feelings of anxiety?

I'm pretty sure it would completely go away. I mean... I don't usually get worked up over things. If I could just get a decent place to sleep after working all day, and not have to fight with this landlord... yeah, the frustration would be gone. I don't think I'd have any lingering anxiety or anything like that. I'd just go back to normal.
